title: Securities Trading Policy (POL-GE-C.000-0007, V5)

tiers.name: Liontown Personnel
tiers.description: All directors and employees of the Company or the Group, as well as consultants and contractors who have access to sensitive information, and their Connected Persons. Subject to the insider trading prohibition, the four Blackout Periods, any Additional Period, the ban on short term or speculative trading, the ban on hedging unvested equity entitlements, and the clearance requirements for hedging, margin loans and other secured lending, and non-discretionary trading plans.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Key Management Personnel (including any director, executive or otherwise), Executive Employees of the Group, and Connected Persons of either. Additional restriction: must not trade in Company Securities at any time, including in exceptional circumstances, without first obtaining prior written clearance from an Approving Officer.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: A person having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, directly or indirectly, including any director (whether executive or otherwise). A component of Restricted Persons.

tiers.name: Executive Employees
tiers.description: Executive employees of the Group. A component of Restricted Persons.

tiers.name: Connected Person
tiers.description: A spouse or partner, child or step-child under 18 years, an unlisted body corporate which the Liontown Personnel controls or is a director of, a trust of which the Liontown Personnel is a trustee and of which he or she or any of the above is a beneficiary, or any other person over whom the Liontown Personnel has significant influence or control. Where the policy requires a Restricted Person to do an act, the Restricted Person must do that act in respect of the Connected Person.

tiers.name: director or officer
tiers.description: Directors and officers of the Company, for the purposes of identifying the Approving Officer under section 8(b).

tiers.name: Managing Director
tiers.description: The Managing Director, who is the Approving Officer for employees but must himself obtain clearance from the Chair or, in the Chair's absence, the Chair of the Audit Committee.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The Chair, who is the Approving Officer for directors and officers but must himself obtain clearance from the Lead Independent Director or the Chair of the Audit Committee.

tiers.name: employees, and other parties identified by the Company from time to time
tiers.description: Employees and other parties the Company identifies as subject to the policy, for the purposes of identifying the Approving Officer under section 8(a).

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board (or its delegate) may impose an Additional Period from time to time, for example because the Company is considering matters that would require disclosure to the market but for Listing Rule 3.1A. It is confidential: 'Liontown Personnel must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.' Blackout Periods and Additional Periods together are Prohibited Periods; trading in an Additional Period is possible only on exceptional circumstances clearance under section 8.

rules.detail: Company Securities expressly include derivatives of shares, options and performance rights, naming equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, whether cash settled or otherwise. Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities at any time without prior written clearance, so an OTC put or written call requires clearance regardless of whether a Prohibited Period is running.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise, (Company Securities). ... Restricted Persons must not trade in Company Securities at any time, including in the exceptional circumstances referred to in section 7, unless the Restricted Person first obtains prior written clearance

rules.detail: For Liontown Personnel who are not Restricted Persons there is no blanket clearance requirement; derivatives over Company Securities are Company Securities and so may not be traded during a Blackout Period or Additional Period or while holding Inside Information, and clearance is required only where the policy stipulates it (sections 7, 12, 13 and 14). A collar is a hedging arrangement, so section 12 clearance would in practice apply to this tier too.
rules.evidence: Liontown Personnel, who are not Restricted Persons, must also adhere to the procedures for obtaining prior written clearance outlined in this Clause where stipulated by this Policy.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no clearance route, on transactions or arrangements limiting the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration scheme. This is a separate sentence from the clearance-based rule for hedging security holdings generally, so no Approving Officer can authorise it.
rules.evidence: Liontown Personnel are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.

rules.detail: Hedging of a vested, unrestricted security holding in the Company is expressly permitted with prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer under the section 8 procedure. The clearance request form has a dedicated field requiring details where section 12 applies, so hedging is contemplated rather than merely tolerated. Clearance may be refused in absolute discretion.
rules.evidence: Liontown Personnel must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 8.

rules.detail: Vested securities held under ASX restricted securities rules or voluntary escrow cannot be traded while the escrow runs, so no physically settled hedge, transfer or pledge of those shares is possible. A cash-settled hedge over them is still a section 12 arrangement requiring clearance, and an Approving Officer would need to be satisfied it does not breach the escrow terms.
rules.evidence: Any Liontown Personnel who holds Company Securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) must comply with the terms of any applicable escrow arrangements and will be unable to trade in those securities during that time.

rules.detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. A prepaid forward or equivalent is an agreement to dispose of securities and so a trade, and it operates to limit the economic risk of the holding, so it needs section 12 clearance; if it is funded by security over the shares it also needs section 13 clearance.
rules.evidence: To "trade" in securities means, whether as principal or agent, to apply for, acquire or dispose of securities; enter into an agreement to apply for, acquire or dispose of securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy. It falls within the ban on short term or speculative trading of Company Securities in section 11, which has no clearance route and no stated exceptions.
rules.evidence: The Company wishes to encourage Liontown Personnel to adopt a long-term attitude to investment in Company Securities. Therefore, Liontown Personnel must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned. The definition of trade covers only applying for, acquiring or disposing of securities and agreements to do so, so a stock loan is caught only to the extent it involves an outright transfer of title, and section 13 addresses secured lending to the person rather than lending of securities by the person.

CFDs are not named but are derivatives of Company shares settled by cash and so are Company Securities; trading them requires clearance for Restricted Persons and is barred in Prohibited Periods for everyone. In practice a CFD would also be caught by the section 11 prohibition on short term or speculative trading.
rules.evidence: derivatives of any of the above (including equity swaps, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options) whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Margin loans in relation to Company Securities are permitted but only with prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer under the section 8 procedure. There is no outright ban, no vesting-state limit and no stated LVR or price trigger guidance. A disposal resulting from the secured lender exercising its rights is excluded from the Blackout Period restrictions by section 9(g).
rules.evidence: Liontown Personnel must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section8.

rules.detail: Granting security over Company Securities is regulated only through section 13, which requires prior written clearance for margin loan agreements and other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities. Granting a charge, lien or pledge unconnected with a lending arrangement is not named and is not within the definition of trade. Securities under ASX restriction or voluntary escrow cannot be encumbered in breach of those arrangements.
rules.evidence: Liontown Personnel must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer

rules.detail: Section 13 is a clearance gate rather than a prohibition and extends beyond margin loans to 'other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities', which captures a bank loan secured on collared shares. Clearance is at the Approving Officer's absolute discretion, is valid for 3 business days by default and can be withdrawn before the dealing is lodged. The clearance request form requires details where section 13 applies.
rules.evidence: If section 12, 13 or 14 of the Company's Share Trading Policy apply please provide details. (Hedging transactions, margin loans and other secured lending or non-discretionary trading plans.)

rules.detail: Ban on short term or speculative trading of Company Securities. No holding period, matching basis, months or carve-outs are specified, so the test is qualitative and applied by the Approving Officer when clearance is sought.
rules.evidence: Therefore, Liontown Personnel must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.

exceptions.evidence: Liontown Personnel, who is not in possession of Inside Information, may request prior written clearance to trade in Company Securities during a Prohibited Period ... where the person is in severe financial hardship; ... A person may be in severe financial hardship if he or she has a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the relevant Company Securities.

A circumstance may be considered exceptional, including but not limited to if the person in question is required by a court order or a court enforceable undertaking to transfer or sell, or accept a transfer of, the Company Securities or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement for them to do so.

a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement. Note section 13 of this policy requires that Liontown Personnel must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer

transfers of Company Securities between a Restricted Person and their spouse, civil partner, dependent child, dependent step-child, family company, family trust or other close family member or of Company Securities already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Restricted Person is a beneficiary;

an investment in, or trading in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in Company Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party;

exceptions.approver: prior written clearance required to put the plan in place
exceptions.evidence: trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this policy and where: (a) the Restricted Person did not enter into the plan or amend the plan during a Prohibited Period; and (b) the trading plan does not permit the Restricted Person to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade;
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer; a disposal of Company Securities arising from a scheme of arrangement;

trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders such as, a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.

the exercise, automatic exercise or automatic conversion of Company Securities issued under an employee incentive scheme. The prohibition does, however, apply to the sale of shares acquired under an employee incentive scheme and also to the sale of shares acquired following the exercise of an option or performance right granted under an employee incentive scheme;
the application for, agreement to acquire and acquisition under such application or agreement of, Company Securities under an employee incentive scheme;

where a Restricted Person is a trustee, trading in the Company Securities by that trust provided that the Restricted Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a Prohibited Period outside a Trading Window is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Restricted Person;
any other circumstances as the Board permits.

financing_disclosure: Liontown Personnel (all tiers); trigger: inception of any margin loan or other secured lending arrangement in relation to Company Securities, and of any hedging arrangement; to the appropriate Approving Officer via the prior written clearance request form, which requires details where section 12, 13 or 14 applies; deadline: before entering into the arrangement.
Restricted Persons; trigger: grant of written clearance; to the Company Secretary for the register of clearances, which is reported to the next Board meeting; deadline: unspecified.

Directors; trigger: any change in Company Securities held directly or indirectly, including a change caused by a secured lender's enforcement or by physical settlement; to the Company Secretary; deadline: as soon as reasonably possible and in any event no later than three business days after the change.

ASX restricted securities agreements and voluntary escrow arrangements (referred to in section 10 but not attached)
exemption_authority: An Approving Officer may, in absolute discretion, grant prior written clearance to trade during a Prohibited Period in exceptional circumstances, being severe financial hardship or other circumstances deemed exceptional by that Approving Officer, including a court order, court enforceable undertaking or other overriding legal or regulatory requirement. The Board may also permit 'any other circumstances' to be treated as trading excluded from section 6 (section 9(o)). Refusal is final and binding and must be kept confidential.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured lending is clearance-gated, not banned
bespoke_clauses.clause: Liontown Personnel must not enter into margin loan agreements or other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer in accordance with the procedure set out in section 8.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is expressly permitted subject to prior written clearance rather than prohibited, which is the single most important difference from policies that ban secured financing outright.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedging is clearance-gated for vested holdings
bespoke_clauses.clause: Liontown Personnel must not enter into transactions or arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in the Company without first obtaining prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The put and call legs are permissible with clearance over vested unrestricted shares, and the clearance form has a dedicated field for section 12 details, so the structure must be disclosed to the Approving Officer in full.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Liontown Personnel are prohibited from entering into transactions or arrangements which limit the economic risk of participating in unvested entitlements under any equity based remuneration schemes.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar must be sized strictly to vested shares; no Approving Officer discretion can cure a hedge that reaches unvested performance rights or options, and over-hedging vested holdings risks being characterised as hedging the unvested tail.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of Company Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excluded from the restrictions outlined in section 6].
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank's enforcement sale is expressly excluded from the Blackout Period restrictions, so lender enforcement during a closed period does not itself breach the policy, though section 8's blanket clearance requirement for Restricted Persons is not in terms disapplied and the carve-out does not displace the insider trading law.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Written clearance can be withdrawn by the Approving Officer at any time prior to the order for dealing being lodged or otherwise authorised, if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing risk sits with the client: a cleared collar can be pulled before execution, so the bank should not commit hedge or funding until the trade is actually lodged.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any written clearance granted under this policy will be valid for the period of 3 business days from the time which it is given or such other period as may be determined by the Approving Officer. The expiry time of the clearance will be stated in the clearance granted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The default execution window is only 3 business days, but the form lets the Approving Officer specify a longer bespoke period, which can be requested up front to accommodate documentation and settlement of a collar and loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any request for written clearance can be given or refused by the Approving Officer in their absolute discretion. ... Where a waiver is refused, it is final and binding on the Restricted Person and the Restricted Person must keep all information relating to the waiver confidential.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no appeal and no reasons requirement, so the bank cannot assume approval of a collar and the client may be unable to explain a refusal to the bank.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Liontown Personnel must not trade in Company Securities within any period imposed by the Board (or its delegate) from time to time ... Liontown Personnel must not disclose to anyone that an Additional Period is in effect.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Undisclosed Additional Periods can block entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement at any time, and the client is barred from telling the bank why.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Liontown Personnel who holds Company Securities subject to binding restrictions on transfer (either as ASX restricted securities or through voluntary escrow arrangements) ... will be unable to trade in those securities during that time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Escrowed shares cannot be delivered to a security trustee or sold on enforcement, so only unrestricted vested shares can serve as collateral for the loan.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Liontown Personnel must not engage in short term or speculative trading of Company Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The prohibition is undefined and qualitative, so a short-dated collar, an early unwind or a cash-settled structure could be characterised as speculative trading in Company Securities, and tenor and settlement mechanics should be raised with the Approving Officer at clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where this policy requires a Restricted Person to do an act or thing, the relevant Restricted Person must do that act or thing in respect of the Connected Person.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the collared shares through a family trust, controlled company or spouse does not avoid the clearance requirements for hedging or secured lending.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If before carrying out the trade, the Restricted Person comes into possession of Inside Information or a Prohibited Period commences, that person must not carry out the trade, notwithstanding that it has been approved.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Approval lapses automatically on the onset of inside information or a blackout, so the bank needs a fresh representation at signing and at each subsequent settlement or roll.

bespoke_clauses.clause: written clearance granted under this policy is never an endorsement of the proposed trade or a confirmation regarding the absence of Inside Information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot rely on the Approving Officer's clearance as diligence and must take its own representations from the client.

summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is unusually accommodating: section 12 permits hedging arrangements that limit the economic risk of a security holding, and section 13 permits margin loans and other secured lending arrangements in relation to Company Securities, in each case subject to prior written clearance from the appropriate Approving Officer rather than being prohibited. The clearance request form has a dedicated field for section 12 and 13 details, so the whole structure must be disclosed; clearance is at absolute discretion, is valid for 3 business days by default (a longer period may be specified), can be withdrawn before the order is lodged, and lapses if inside information arises or a Prohibited Period starts. The collar must be sized strictly to vested holdings, because hedging arrangements limiting the economic risk of unvested equity scheme entitlements are prohibited outright with no clearance route, and escrowed or ASX restricted shares cannot be traded or delivered. Execution must sit outside the four quarterly Blackout Periods and any confidential Board-imposed Additional Period, and Restricted Persons (KMP, executive employees and their Connected Persons) need clearance for every trade including the derivative legs, since Company Securities expressly include over-the-counter options and equity swaps. A helpful feature for the bank is section 9(g), which excludes a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights from the blackout restrictions; tenor should be long enough to avoid the undefined ban on short term or speculative trading, and directors must report resulting holdings changes within three business days.
